knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Spray is kept away from connectors, inverters and junction boxes. Spraying an inverter to cool it or a junction box to rinse it is not acceptable.
Separate equipment prevents cross-contamination and keeps each product to its approved use, so it can also be traced if an incident occurs.

Attachments to pressure equipment need written approval from the manufacturer or a competent person (WorkSafe Victoria jetting alert, published 14 September 2022). A worker does not fit one on the basis that it is a common tool.
Only an approved product with its safety data sheet, used as the manufacturer allows, is consistent with this draft. Unknown or strong products are not acceptable.

practicalCriteria: The learner marks the electrical parts of a demonstration array and keeps the spray away from them.
The learner selects the lowest approved water method, using the supplied manufacturer instructions.
The learner sets up separate, labelled equipment for each product and for clean water.
The learner records the product, its label directions and the safety data sheet reference.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is assessed separately by observation of equipment set-up and spray control. A knowledge pass does not verify spray control on a live array.
evidenceRequired: Record of the electrical parts marked and the spray direction used
Water method and the manufacturer instruction used
Product name, label directions and safety data sheet reference
Record of any water contact with an electrical part and the referral
stopWorkCriteria: The learner aims spray at a junction box or inverter.
The learner uses a jet setting not allowed by the instructions.
The learner uses one brush or bucket for several products.
The learner mixes products to strengthen the clean.
